claims.text: As of 28 July 2026, a total of 109 deaths and 360 injuries have been reported nationwide. The majority of casualties resulted from house collapses and flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall. Additionally, 796 houses have been damaged, either fully or partially, while 379 livestock have perished.

OCHA, 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 2' (as of 10 August 2026, infographic sourced to NDMA's Monsoon situation report covering 26 June-9 August 2026, plus PMD and WFP data): 'Deaths: 153,' 'Injured: 457,' 'Houses Damaged: 1,339 total (432 Fully Damaged and 907 Partially Damaged),' 'Livestock Lost: 576.'

NDMA, Monsoon 2026 Daily Situation Report No. 47 (11 August 2026): cumulative casualties and injuries table, 'From 26 June 2026 to 11 August 2026' -- Grand Total Deceased 155 (52 male, 30 female, 73 children), Grand Total Injured 460 (195 male, 113 female, 152 children). Cumulative damage table for the same period: Houses Full 432, Partial 909, Total 1,341; Livestock Perished 580. The last-24-hours entry for 11 August records 1 injury (Narowal, Punjab), no new deaths, and 1 partial house damaged.

NDMA Monsoon 2026 Daily Situation Report No. 49 (covering 1300 hrs 12 August - 1300 hrs 13 August 2026): cumulative deaths unchanged at 155 (52 male, 30 female, 73 children); injured risen to 468 (up from 460, +8 in the last 24 hours, all in Rajanpur, Punjab); houses damaged (cumulative) risen to 1,345 (432 fully damaged, 913 partially damaged, up from 1,341); livestock perished unchanged at 580; cumulative rescue operations since 26 June 2026: 1,111 operations, 8,700 persons rescued.

OCHA's 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 2' (as of 10 August 2026, sourced from NDMA's situation reporting covering 26 June-9 August 2026): 153 deaths, 457 injured, 1,339 houses damaged (432 fully, 907 partially), 576 livestock lost, with severe impacts in Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. WHO (12 August 2026) states the health sector stands ready to activate the Monsoon and Flood Contingency Plan 2026 to assist 1.8 million people in high-risk areas.

NDMA's live Monsoon 2026 SITREP dashboard, as of 18 August 2026 (cumulative, 26 June-18 August 2026): Grand Total Deceased 161 (54 male, 32 female, 75 children), Grand Total Injured 473 (196 male, 118 female, 159 children) -- up from 155 deaths / 468 injured as of NDMA Daily Situation Report No. 49 (13 August 2026). Cumulative houses damaged 1,355 total (433 fully damaged, 922 partially damaged); livestock perished 585. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa recorded the highest death toll (67) and injury count (92); Punjab recorded 54 deaths and 341 injured; Gilgit-Baltistan recorded the most housing damage (403 structures). Separately, NDMA's numbered Daily Situation Report No. 51 (15 August 2026, covering 1300 hrs 14 August-1300 hrs 15 August 2026), fetched directly, confirms cumulative Grand Total Deceased 157 and Grand Total Injured 469 as of that date, and cumulative houses damaged of 1,349 (433 full, 916 partial) and livestock perished 585 -- consistent with the trend shown on the live dashboard, and reflecting NDMA's own numbered situation-report series had progressed to Report No. 51 without being previously captured in this record. reliefweb.int/country/pak again returned HTTP 403 Forbidden and no OCHA 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 3' was found via search.

NDMA and PDMA Punjab have moved from advisory to an active flood alert for the Chenab, Jhelum and Ravi rivers from 29 July-05 August, with evacuations already being directed in low-lying and riverbank areas.

OCHA's 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 1' infographic (as of 03 Aug 2026, posted to ReliefWeb 3 August 2026) states: 'Based on NDMA Monsoon situation report covering from 26 June to 2 August 2026, monsoon-related incidents have resulted in 126 deaths and 416 injuries across Pakistan... In addition, 1,119 houses have been damaged (352 fully damaged and 767 partially damaged), while 508 livestock have perished due to the monsoon-related hazards. The most affected areas in terms of housing damage include Gilgit-Baltistan, Balochistan, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and AJ&K.'

description: Heavy monsoon rains beginning 26 June 2026 have triggered flash floods, riverine flooding and house collapses across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, Gilgit-Baltistan, Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Balochistan and Sindh. Pakistan's National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) records a cumulative 161 deaths and 473 injuries nationwide from 26 June to 18 August 2026, with 1,355 houses damaged and 585 livestock lost; Khyber Pakhtunkhwa carries the heaviest provincial death toll at 67, Punjab the most injuries at 341, and Gilgit-Baltistan the most housing damage at 403 structures. Casualties stem mainly from house collapses, flash floods, drowning and electrocution. NDMA continues to log new casualties and damage daily — its teams had carried out 1,111 rescue operations and rescued 8,700 people by 13 August — relief operations remain active in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu & Kashmir, and WHO stands ready to activate a contingency plan to assist 1.8 million people in high-risk areas.

updates.text: NDMA's live Monsoon 2026 SITREP dashboard raised the cumulative toll to 161 deaths and 473 injuries as of 18 August, up from 155 deaths and 468 injuries in Daily Situation Report No. 49 (13 August); cumulative houses damaged rose to 1,355 and livestock perished to 585. Daily Situation Report No. 51 (15 August) had recorded an intermediate 157 deaths and 469 injuries.

NDMA Daily Situation Report No. 49 recorded deaths unchanged at 155 while injuries rose to 468 (up 8, all in Rajanpur, Punjab) and cumulative house damage reached 1,345; rescue teams had conducted 1,111 operations and rescued 8,700 people since 26 June.

OCHA's Monsoon Situation Update 2 (as of 10 August) recorded 153 deaths and 457 injuries, and NDMA's Daily Situation Report No. 47 (11 August) put the cumulative toll at 155 deaths, 460 injuries, 1,341 houses damaged and 580 livestock lost — up from 126 deaths and 416 injuries as of 3 August.
WHO said the health sector stands ready to activate the Monsoon and Flood Contingency Plan 2026 to assist 1.8 million people in high-risk areas.

OCHA's Monsoon Situation Update 1 (as of 3 August, sourced to NDMA reporting for 26 June-2 August) recorded 126 deaths and 416 injuries nationwide, with 1,119 houses damaged and 508 livestock lost — up from 109 deaths and 360 injuries reported as of 28 July.
NDMA and PDMA Punjab moved from an advisory to an active flood alert for the Chenab, Jhelum and Ravi rivers for 29 July-5 August, directing evacuations in low-lying and riverbank areas.
